decisions.statement: A cost is taken around one run rather than around every run one call makes.
A line states the run a cost was taken in.
A line names whatever ran.
The paths counted are the change's own rather than the paths the check judged.
A run is timed by the processor rather than by the clock alone.
The seconds a reaped child burned are read from `/proc/self/stat`.
A child still running when a run closes is reaped nowhere yet.
The kernel counts nothing of such a child there.
The seconds such a child burned are read from that child's own `/proc` entry.
Every descendant is read rather than the children alone.
A child's own entry states that child's seconds rather than its children's.
A live child's reaped seconds are read nowhere here.
Every run a process makes is a child of that process.
The reaped seconds and the live ones are added.
The kernel's count is read before and after the live children are read.
A reading the kernel's count changed across is made again.
A reading is made three times at most.
The high-water mark is forgotten before a run.
The mark after a run is that run's own peak.
A peak read from a mark no run forgot measures the record rather than the run.
A line states whether the mark was forgotten.
A proxy is never read as a measurement.
The memory a run added is that run's peak over the memory resident when the run opened.
A run states the count of reads and writes that run made and the bytes that run read.
Those counts are read from `/proc/self/io` as the seconds are read from `/proc/self/stat`.
The bytes counted are the bytes a run asked for rather than the bytes a disk fetched.
A run made wholly in a child is recorded from what the kernel said of that child.
Every second such a run spent is a child's, so the recorder's own seconds are none.
A child starts holding nothing.
The memory such a run added is that run's whole peak.
Such a run states whether the peak it reached was measured.
A line says of such a peak what the run stating it says.
The reads and writes such a run made are counted nowhere.
The property a line is kept under is named by the caller recording that line.
A caller naming no property is kept under `entries`.
Every line was kept under `entries` before.
A line is appended to the last numbered file rather than rewriting that file.
A line rolls into the next numbered file where the ceiling is reached.
A file's fill is read from its size rather than from its text.
Nothing here refuses a run for that run's cost.
Closing a cost and minting its run id and appending its line are one call.
A disk that refuses a line for a page that is there leaves the run's answer alone.
A line for a path naming no page refuses the run rather than being dropped.
The two are told apart by whether the page named is there.
The peak memory a reaped child reached is read nowhere here.
A run's peak has the memory earlier runs left resident.
A peak a run within forgot is no peak of the run around that run.
A writer takes the turn over a page's first entry file before reading a fill.
The turn is given up once the line has reached the file.
A line whose turn has not come in five seconds is dropped.
A line whose next file cannot be named is appended to the full file rather than refused.
A line that is no cost is appended beside a page the same way a cost is.

definition: what one run cost, appended beside the page of what ran
